- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, particularly in first 7–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 5–10%.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias in 10–15 day horizon — if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward.
- In 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term downward trend after sustained negative sentiment; add 2–3% downward bias if sentiment remains negative for 5+ days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast upward by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.
